questions.stem: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: The unit of resistance is the ohm. One ohm is the resistance when a potential difference of 1 V drives a current of 1 A through the component.

questions.stem: A resistor has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 4 A flowing through it. What is its resistance?
questions.explanation: Using R = V/I: R = 12 V / 4 A = 3 ohms. Resistance equals the potential difference divided by the current.

questions.stem: What happens to the resistance of a wire if its length is doubled (all other factors remaining the same)?
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to the length of a wire (R = rho x L/A). Doubling the length doubles the resistance because charge carriers must travel further through the material.

questions.stem: What happens to the resistance of a wire if its cross-sectional area is doubled?
questions.explanation: Resistance is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area of a wire (R = rho x L/A). A larger area provides more space for charge carriers to flow, so doubling the area halves the resistance.

questions.stem: Three resistors of 2 ohms, 3 ohms, and 5 ohms are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: In a series circuit, total resistance is the sum of all individual resistances: R_total = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 ohms.

questions.stem: Two resistors of equal resistance R are connected in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel: 1/R_total = 1/R + 1/R = 2/R, so R_total = R/2. The combined resistance of parallel resistors is always less than the smallest individual resistance.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT affect the resistance of a wire?

options.text: The material the wire is made from
The current flowing through the wire
The cross-sectional area of the wire

questions.explanation: The resistance of a wire depends on its length, cross-sectional area, material (resistivity), and temperature. For an ohmic conductor, resistance is independent of the current flowing through it.
